findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify AC6's check MECHANISM and a positive rationale for it: state whether it verifies Terraform-state parity or true production in-service state, and make it diff the DECLARED set against an AWS/in-service signal (e.g. gate_scratch_mounted==1, alarms present with recorded state, docker cap IN EFFECT) rather than only asserting `terraform plan` shows no changes — since applied-but-not-mounted is the actual S1 failure a plan-diff cannot detect.
evidence: AC6 text: 'A CHECK exists that distinguishes "declared in Terraform" from "provisioned in AWS"... Note the Terraform Drift workflow is the natural home, but it is itself defective... Whatever is built must not depend on that being fixed first' — names a constraint and a home but no mechanism and no positive rationale.

The epic's own history (ticket comments; user_data.sh:216-238; observability.sh:351-354) shows S1's volume WAS applied/attached in Terraform yet never mounted — gate_scratch_mounted read 0 on every datapoint. A plan-diff-based check (declared == applied) would have reported CLEAN for exactly that failure, because Terraform only attaches a raw block device; formatting/mount/markers come from cloud-init, outside Terraform state.

A structurally different alternative not considered in the plan: assert the in-service SIGNAL from AWS/CloudWatch directly (gate_scratch_mounted==1, the five alarms exist with recorded non-INSUFFICIENT_DATA state, docker-storage cap reports IN EFFECT) and diff that against the Terraform-declared set — this catches applied-but-not-in-service, which 'terraform plan shows no changes' cannot.
findings.finding: AC6 (the declared-vs-provisioned CHECK) is the plan's only genuine design deliverable, but it neither commits to a mechanism nor states a positive rationale for one — and the most obvious mechanism (re-run `terraform plan` and assert no changes) detects only DECLARED-vs-APPLIED drift, not the actual S1/S2 failure the epic is about, which is APPLIED-but-NOT-IN-SERVICE (volume attached yet never mounted, gate_scratch_mounted stuck at 0).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria → AC6; Verification → 'The declared-vs-provisioned check is a code change...'
scenarios: Implementer builds AC6 as a `terraform plan`-diff assertion; a future story again declares+applies an EBS attachment but the on-box mount silently fails; the check reports green and the exact S1 shape recurs — the outcome AC6 exists to prevent.
Reviewer/operator cannot tell from the plan whether AC6 is meant to verify Terraform-state parity or true production in-service state, so the built check may solve a proxy.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide explicitly whether the AC6 declared-vs-provisioned check should be a separate child/ticket from the operator-gated provisioning (AC1-AC5), since the code guardrail is independently valuable, testable, and releasable on a different timeline than the manual apply/restart.
evidence: AC5 is gated on an operator scheduling 'systemctl restart docker ... in a quiet window'; AC1 apply is gated on operator approval ('Not applying Terraform outside operator approval').
AC6 is a separate code deliverable: 'The declared-vs-provisioned check is a code change that must pass local verification and Gerrit review before this ticket closes.'
The check's value (preventing silent recurrence) is independent of whether this specific apply/mount/restart completes.
findings.finding: The ticket bundles two concerns with distinct reasons-to-change and independent releasability: (a) a one-time, operator-gated provisioning run — Terraform apply, on-box mount runbook, daemon restart (AC1-AC5), all manual ops verified by AWS/on-box checks, blocked on operator approval and a quiet window; and (b) a durable code-level guardrail — the declared-vs-provisioned CHECK (AC6), a Gerrit-reviewed code change that prevents future recurrence regardless of whether this particular apply happens. The check is independently valuable and testable and could ship (and catch future S1/S2-shape gaps) even if the provisioning is delayed by operator scheduling; conversely the provisioning delivers its value without the check. This mixes a manual-ops increment with a code deliverable on different timelines.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC1-AC5 (provisioning) vs AC6 (declared-vs-provisioned check)
